report_title: Phase 7 Deduplication, Class Balancing, and Experimental Dataset Creation Report

methodology.deduplication_rule: Exact content matching across all 10 core event features (event_type, source, severity, source_ip, dest_ip, source_port, dest_port, protocol, user, raw_log), keeping the first occurrence.
methodology.sampling_method: Stratified proportional sampling across all 12 benign event types with random_state=42

data_leakage_and_shortcut_mitigation.deterministic_event_type_leak: event_type == 'auth_failure' is 100% predictive of class 1. Policy: Preserved in dataset as metadata/evaluation target; must be excluded from model input prompts.
data_leakage_and_shortcut_mitigation.host_shortcut_mitigation: Suspicious events originate strictly from HOST-0002 (23) and HOST-0006 (21). Policy: Must use host-grouped splitting or hostname masking for future training.
data_leakage_and_shortcut_mitigation.grouped_splitting_requirement: Splits must be template-aware and host-grouped to test actual generalization rather than token memorization.

final_experimental_assessment.suitability_for_qwen3_4b_fine_tuning: Conditionally suitable as a proof-of-concept / binary triage baseline only.
core_limitations: Extremely small sample size (484 records total) for a 4B parameter language model.
Zero variety in the suspicious class: all 44 records represent a single auth_failure syslog template.
Zero examples of confirmed malicious attacks (class 2 is unpopulated in this slice).
High risk of overfitting to the specific syslog duration/counter syntax unless supplemented with upstream events.
